extracted.intended_audience: researchers and investigators seeking Parkinson's Research Program (PRP) funding through the CDMRP; program applicants and stakeholders (service members, veterans, clinicians, PD researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the CDMRP Parkinson's Research Program (PRP) goals, scope, and evaluation context to guide prospective applicants about what kinds of Parkinson's disease research the program seeks to fund and how proposals are considered. Includes program vision/mission, scope change from NETP to PRP, and links to review and application resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Vision — clinically meaningful treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision – To improve the health and lives of people with, or at risk for, Parkinson’s disease through innovative research that translates to clinically meaningful treatments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should align proposals with the program vision by proposing innovative research with clear pathways to translation into clinically meaningful treatments that improve health or quality of life for people with or at risk for PD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Mission — high-impact research addressing risk, progression, or symptoms
rubrics_metrics.description: Mission – To support high-impact research that intends to decrease risk, slow progression, or ease symptoms of Parkinson's disease that benefit Service Members and their Families, Veterans and the general public
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should target one or more of the mission goals (decrease risk, slow progression, ease symptoms) and demonstrate potential benefit to Service Members and their Families, Veterans, and/or the general public. Emphasis is on 'high-impact' outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — all types of Parkinson's disease research (expanded from NETP)
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY22, Congress transitioned the Neurotoxin Exposure Treatment Parkinson's (NETP) program to the Parkinson's Research Program (PRP) and broadened the research from neurotoxin exposure treatment PD research to all types of PD research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program accepts projects across the full spectrum of PD research (not limited to neurotoxin exposure). Applicants whose work focuses on toxic exposure research are directed to the Toxic Exposures Research Program, but PRP's scope is broad across PD-related topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority — advance understanding of disease with the ultimate goal of ending PD
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRP challenges the scientific community to develop the most impactful research that will advance the understanding of the disease, with the ultimate goal of ending PD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded projects are expected to advance basic or clinical understanding in ways that move the field toward ending Parkinson's disease; proposals should articulate how the work will be impactful and advance understanding rather than being purely incremental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended beneficiaries — benefit Service Members, families, Veterans, and the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Mission wording specifies beneficiaries: 'Service Members and their Families, Veterans and the general public.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should, where appropriate, explain the anticipated benefit of their research to these populations (e.g., relevance to military or Veteran exposures, applicability to family/caregiver needs, or broad public health impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation mechanism — two‑tiered review process and programs of peer/programmatic panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Review (site contains links including 'Two Tiered Review Process', 'Programmatic Panels', 'Peer Review Participants', and 'Programmatic Panels: FY24, Previous Years').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals to the PRP are evaluated through CDMRP's two-tiered review (typically peer review followed by programmatic review). Applicants should consult the program's review guidance (e.g., peer review criteria, programmatic considerations, consumer involvement) to tailor applications to the evaluation process.
